newsitem.title: USA: NYS comptroller lifts ban on Swiss banks.
newsitem.headline: NYS comptroller lifts ban on Swiss banks.

text.p: The New York State Comptroller on Wednesday said a ban stopping the state from using Swiss banks for overnight investments due to concerns about how they had treated Holocaust victims had been removed.
"Based on the recommendation of the World Jewish Congress, the comptroller has lifted the ban," said a spokeswoman for the comptroller, H. Carl McCall.
The ban was put in place as of January 30, and the state comptroller at that time anticipated that it would last until investigations into the treatment of the Holocaust victims were completed.
McCall is the trustee of the state's approximately $80 billion pension fund.

The Swiss government on Wednesday gave final approval to a Holocaust memorial fund that gives international Jewish groups a big say in how to distribute millions of dollars in humanitarian aid to Holocaust victims.

The World Jewish Congress, which has led international criticism of Swiss banks and the Swiss financial role in World War Two, welcomed the decision as a big step towards better Jewish-Swiss relations after months of bitter wrangling.
